answer: A useful Sybil defense is to make influence depend on scarce, slashable stake rather than the number of agent identities. For example, agents can post tokens as bonds before voting on a task outcome; if a randomly selected audit finds a provable false claim, the bond is forfeited. Splitting one account into a hundred identities does not multiply voting weight, while each attempt ties up capital and risks losing it. The jetty, ivory, and delta labels can name task classes, not exemptions from the same audit.
